artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

artifacts.title: Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Complainants alleged Missouri Presbytery erred in failing to find a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held views contrary to the Westminster Standards in its BCO 31-2 investigation. The SJC found that MOP erred but declared the case moot because MOP had already conducted a trial of TE Meyers during the pendency of the case before the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: Susan Elizabeth Spann filed an appeal alleging Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church committed excommunication without process and spiritual abuse, but the SJC dismissed the appeal as premature because there was no record of a judicial decision by OMPC nor any prior appeal to Evangel Presbytery as required by BCO 42-2. The SJC requested that Evangel Presbytery direct OMPC to provide a written response to Ms. Spann's concerns.

artifacts.title: Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Paul Armes's complaint on the grounds that his excommunication removed his standing; the SJC unanimously remanded the case to the Presbytery after the Presbytery conceded error, holding that even an excommunicated person retains standing to complain against the censure itself.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that McNeil's appeal was judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial, having refused to enter a plea or appear before Chesapeake Presbytery's Judicial Commission, and that his subsequent censure of suspension from the sacraments eliminated his standing to file further complaints against post-censure actions of the court.

artifacts.title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: Dr. Robert Shive appealed his conviction and excommunication after Christ Covenant Church found him guilty of sinful and sexually inappropriate speech toward two patients. The SJC found no reversible error in the trial, but held that the record did not show contumacy or impenitence sufficient for excommunication, reversed that censure, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5; a dissent was recorded.

artifacts.title: Meaning of willful neglect and gross crime under BCO 46-5 and 30-4

matches.evidence: BCO 46-5 requires due process under BCO 27-5 for incorrigible members, and 'gross crime or heresy' is to be understood in its biblical and moral sense as determined by the church court.
